title: You’ve heard it before.
paragraphs: And if you’re honest, part of you liked how it sounded. Fair. Clean. Balanced. Someone hurts you… they should feel it too. No one gets away with anything.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
That phrase was never permission for revenge.
It was a restraint on it.
Picture the world when those words were first spoken.

Violence wasn’t measured—it escalated. Someone steals from you, you wipe out their family. Someone injures you, you take their life. Justice wasn’t justice. It was spiraling vengeance dressed up as honor.
“Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.” — Exodus 21:24

Not more than an eye.
Not more than a tooth.
God wasn’t fueling revenge—He was putting a leash on it.
He was saying: You don’t get to go beyond what was done to you.
Because He knew something about the human heart.
You want to feel powerful again.

What they said.
What they did.
How it stayed in your head long after it was over.
And something inside you whispered, They deserve it.
You replayed it, didn’t you? Imagined what you’d say next time. How you’d win. How they’d finally feel small.
That’s where “eye for an eye” gets twisted.
Because your heart doesn’t stop at equal.
And He doesn’t soften the law.
“You have heard that it was said, ‘Eye for eye, and tooth for tooth.’ But I tell you, do not resist an evil person…” — Matthew 5:38–39
He’s confronting your addiction to retaliation.
He’s saying: You’re not as righteous as you think you are.
Because even when you’ve been wronged…
Your response reveals what owns you.
Because if justice is truly equal…
Not what they did to you.

The lies.
The hidden thoughts.
The pride you protect.
The moments you knew were wrong—and still chose them.
If it’s truly “eye for an eye”… then what is owed for your sin?
“For the wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23
We love justice—until it points at us.

He doesn’t ignore sin.
He doesn’t sweep it away.
So where does that leave you?
Jesus didn’t cancel “eye for an eye.”
“But He was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our iniquities… and by His wounds we are healed.” — Isaiah 53:5
This is the part most people never sit with long enough.
God didn’t become unjust to forgive you.
On the cross, justice and mercy collided.
And Jesus stood in your place.
Not because you balanced the scales.
But because grace stepped in where you couldn’t.
If you’ve been forgiven like that…
What right do you have to hold onto revenge?
“But if you do not forgive others their sins, your Father will not forgive your sins.” — Matthew 6:15
You can’t receive mercy and still demand payback.
You can’t cling to grace and still thirst for revenge.
This is where it gets personal.
A name just came to mind.
There are two paths in front of you.

One keeps score.
Replays wounds.
Feeds anger.
And slowly hardens you.

The other releases.
Not because they deserve it—
But because you didn’t either.
One keeps you chained to the past.
The other leads you to the cross.
There’s more to this than just understanding it once.

If you stay where you are, your heart will drift back to old patterns. That’s what it does. But if you walk deeper—if you keep exposing, confronting, and renewing your mind with truth—you won’t stay stuck in cycles that are quietly destroying you.
Follow it. Stay with it. Let it challenge you again and again.
And if you’re ready to go deeper into real, Scripture-rooted transformation, step into it here:
You’ll need to come back to it the next time that feeling rises again.
And next time… you’ll know what to do.
